architecture.name: VerificationScriptExportSurface
architecture.responsibility: Export approved manifest verification contracts into deterministic root-runnable scripts and a reviewable index.

design.dataModels: VerificationScriptExportSummary stores supported task types, unsupported task types, exportedScripts, and skippedTasks. Each exported script descriptor contains the manifest task, safe argv, verification contract, and generated script path.
performanceConstraints: The export command performs local file reads and writes only.
Generated scripts run focused validation commands rather than the full health gate.
securityConsiderations: Manual prose and unsupported commands remain skipped with reasons.
design.sequenceDiagram:
sequenceDiagram
  participant Operator
  participant Anvilctl
  participant NativeCLI
  participant Exporter
  Operator->>Anvilctl: verification-scripts-export --worktree
  Anvilctl->>NativeCLI: --workspace-verification-scripts-export
  NativeCLI->>Exporter: export(bundle, worktreeURL)
  Exporter-->>NativeCLI: VerificationScriptExportSummary
  NativeCLI-->>Anvilctl: JSON summary
  Anvilctl-->>Operator: JSON or human summary

tasks.description: Run exporter unit tests from the repository root.
tasks.title: Verify exporter

tasks.description: Run runner unit tests from the repository root.
tasks.title: Verify runner

tasks.description: Run the CLI contract that proves anvilctl writes scripts, index, README, and skipped reasons.
tasks.title: Verify CLI export

tasks.description: Run the repository artifact guard that decodes the spec bundle and exported verification index.
tasks.title: Verify repo artifacts

tasks.description: Inspect exportedScripts and skippedTasks in the generated index.
tasks.title: Manual export boundary review
tasks.verificationContract: Review .anvil/bin/verification-tasks.json and confirm exportedScripts and skippedTasks.

requirements.rationale: Generated verification scripts are runnable local code.
requirements.target: Only SafeCommandParser-approved single-line commands are written as executable scripts.
requirements.title: Safe command export only

requirements.rationale: The exporter scripts cd to the workspace root before invoking their command.
requirements.target: Exported scripts run from the repository root.
requirements.title: Root-runnable scripts

nonFunctionalRequirements.summary: The export path must be deterministic, safe to inspect, and bounded to local verification commands.

notDoingList: No live LLM or credential checks.
No full make anvil-health gate unless focused validation exposes a broader regression.
rawIntent: Export deterministic verification scripts for this anvil_opencode workspace from the approved .anvil/specs bundle.

observabilityChecks: Human anvilctl output lists exported scripts and skipped reasons.
git check-ignore reports only allowlist negation entries for the index and bundle.
rollbackSteps: Remove the CLI wrapper and generated .anvil/bin artifacts.
rolloutSteps: Run anvilctl verification-scripts-export against the workspace.
releaseReadiness.summary: Ship this slice after focused exporter, runner, CLI, repository artifact, real export, ignore-boundary, and generated-script checks pass.

risks.description: A prompt-style or compound command could be written as a runnable script.
risks.title: Unsafe command persistence

risks.description: .anvil/bin or .anvil/specs/bundle.json remains ignored, hiding proof from review.
mitigation: Unignore only the spec bundle, README, index, and generated verification scripts.
risks.title: Unreviewable generated proof

riskRegister.summary: Unsafe commands must remain skipped and generated proof must be reviewable.

stories.title: Maintainer Export Deterministic Verification Scripts
stories.narrative: As a maintainer I want export deterministic verification scripts from the approved workspace spec so that verification can be rerun without an agent loop or GUI-only action

criteria.then: .anvil/bin/verification-tasks.json, README.md, and executable verify scripts are written

criteria.given: a task has unsupported manual prose
criteria.then: the task appears in skippedTasks with a reason

stories.title: Maintainer Review Export Artifacts
stories.narrative: As a maintainer I want keep generated verification export artifacts reviewable so that reviewers can see exactly what was exported and skipped

assumptions: No live LLM, credential, production, or GUI-only path is required.

heuristics: Reuse existing exporter and runner behavior.
decisions.rationale: The exporter already owns script rendering, safe-command filtering, skipped-task accounting, and JSON index shape.
decisions.title: Headless verification script export

decisions.chosenOption: Unignore only the spec bundle and .anvil/bin verification artifacts.
decisions.rationale: The repo needs reviewable proof of what was exported while preserving local runtime privacy.
decisions.title: Track generated proof artifacts

strategy.summary: Use the existing VerificationScriptExporter and VerificationScriptRunner as the implementation, with a narrow terminal export surface for reproducible workspace generation.

sensitiveAssets: Local environment variables available to test commands
threatModel.summary: Generated verification scripts are local executable artifacts and must not turn arbitrary prose or compound shell text into code.

threats.abuseCase: A compound shell command or manual prose contract is persisted as executable code.
threats.title: Unsafe command export

threats.abuseCase: Operators run scripts without seeing which tasks were skipped.
controls: Persist exportedScripts and skippedTasks in the index and README.
threats.title: Hidden export boundary
verification: Decode verification-tasks.json and report both arrays.

layers.scope: Exporter script rendering and skipped-task accounting
layers.title: Exporter behavior

layers.scope: Repository spec bundle and verification index
layers.title: Repository artifact contract

verificationPlan.summary: Validate exporter, runner, CLI, repository artifact, real export, ignore-boundary, and generated-script behavior.
